clue.text: Plug image, keeping fit

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: spit is image, as in the spitting image or 'the very spit of'
a fit is a bout or turn, and so is a go

explanation.surface: Someone shopping for a plug wants a picture of one that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or tap that stops the vent of a cask, so a kind of plug.

clue.text: Soft article under current in river

indicators.note: in means these letters sit inside the river name

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the article comes below the current letter

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A gentle object lies beneath the flow of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction meaning softly or soft, used in scores.

clue.text: Piety from Democrat on policy stopping chitchat

indicators.note: stopping means the inner letters plug the chitchat word like a stopper

parts.note: goss is informal British slang for gossip or chitchat

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the Democrat letter sits above the policy word

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A Democrat's stance on faith halts idle chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSS is a British informal clipping of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Godliness is devoutness, piety, being godly in conduct.

clue.text: Speech getting stick, with length cut, following fashion

indicators.note: following means the trimmed stick word comes after the fashion word

parts.note: ton is fashion or style, as in 'the ton', high society

indicators.note: cut means a letter is removed from the stick word

parts.note: glue sticks, so glue is stick

explanation.surface: A speaker is criticised for cutting short a fashionable talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language or speech, as in the mother tongue.

clue.text: Ecstatic about bit of money that's settled matter

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: sent is a dated slang word for ecstatic, carried away
a dime is a ten-cent coin, a small bit of American money

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a little cash has settled the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that has settled to the bottom of a liquid, a literal reading of the phrase.

clue.text: Act formally trained censor may not end

indicators.note: trained means the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A trained censor might never stop acting formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is the idiom for behaving with strict formality.

clue.text: Taunting upset father in disreputable bar

indicators.note: in places the turned father word inside the bar word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable bar

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the father word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Jeering at an upset father in a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisive means mocking or scornful, which is what taunting is.

clue.text: Cut second link

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
to wed is to link or join, as in marriage

explanation.surface: A film editor makes a cut and a second link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowed is the past tense of mow, to cut grass, so the verb cut in its past form.

clue.text: See English character giving up right after refusal in romance?

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the refusal word

parts.note: no is a refusal
v, for the Latin vide, means see in references

indicators.note: giving up means the character word sheds a letter

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: An English letter-writer gives up on the right after being rejected in love.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a light romance is one kind of short novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, typically a light sentimental love story, so a romance.

clue.text: Fern ahead in ground within westward border

indicators.note: within means the shuffled letters sit inside the border word
westward in an across clue means read right to left, so the border word turns round

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down, signals the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A fern grows out front in soil inside a western boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is not soil here but the past tense of grind, signalling a rearrangement; 'westward' reads right to left in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhair is a delicate fern of the genus Adiantum, so an example of the class named.

clue.text: Signal surrender in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken and we write a different word that sounds the same

parts.note: to waive a right is to surrender it

explanation.surface: A white flag or speech can signal surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave a hand or flag is to signal to someone, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Chaff in heap on the way out

indicators.note: in places the teasing word inside the heap word

parts.note: a mound is a heap or pile
to chaff is to tease, and so is to rib

explanation.surface: Husks in a pile are about to be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means near death or in terminal decline, which is the idiom for being on the way out.

clue.text: Down valley, dropping a load

parts.note: down means sad, low in spirits

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is let fall from the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: A pack animal heads down the valley, shedding its load.
explanation.definitionFit: To saddle someone with a task is to burden or load them with it; both are verbs.

clue.text: With last of business covered, take off for recess

indicators.note: covered means the picked letter is wrapped by the mimicking word

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape them

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Once the last bit of business is dealt with, leave for the break.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Wine, fine mixture in case

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an olio is a mixture or medley

explanation.surface: Wine and a fine blend held in a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat case for carrying papers or drawings.

clue.text: Direct barrier faced by tsar in revolution

indicators.note: faced by means the barrier has the turned name in front of it
in revolution means the name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Ivan was the name of several Russian tsars, including Ivan the Terrible
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A tsar meets a barricade during a revolution and must find a way through.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate a ship or route is to steer or direct it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Surveyor arranged to see digs

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A surveyor fixes a visit to the excavations.
explanation.definitionFit: A geodesist is a surveyor who measures the earth's shape and large areas of its surface.

clue.text: Many cross with inclusion of large gratuity

indicators.note: with inclusion of means the cross word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: Many get angry when a big tip is included.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple means numerous, many, as in multiple injuries.

clue.text: Good to carry on south with small force

indicators.note: to carry means the good word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: pure means good, virtuous
re means on or about, as in a letter heading
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Pressing on southward under a small amount of force is the good thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure is force applied to something, physical or figurative, as in pressure to resign.

clue.text: Spread out round enclosure

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Sheep fan out around their fold.
explanation.definitionFit: Open as a verb means unfold or spread out, as a map or a fan is opened.

clue.text: Information in order to make part of engine

indicators.note: in means the information word sits inside the order word

parts.note: to bid is to order or command
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Information in order to build a component of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of an engine's connecting rod, where it joins the crankshaft.

clue.text: Court after blunder not having good influence

indicators.note: after means the court abbreviation comes behind the trimmed blunder
not having means a letter is taken away from the blunder word

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
Ct is the abbreviation for court, as in street names

explanation.surface: A courtier who blundered is left without any good influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect something is to have an influence on it; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Anxious part of Bronze Age reconstruction

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to be part of rebuilding a Bronze Age site.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious in the sense of keen or impatient to do something is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Hole in scheme losing initial support

indicators.note: in means the hole word sits inside the trimmed scheme word
losing initial means the scheme word drops its first letter

parts.note: a device is a scheme or plan
a den is a hole or lair

explanation.surface: A gap in a plan means it loses its first backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing initial' leaves EVICE; 'support' is a verb here, as in to evidence a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is what supports a claim, and to evidence something is to support it with proof.

clue.text: Boast new honour

parts.note: to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: Bragging about a fresh award.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is to honour them, and a crown is the honour of a sovereign or champion.

clue.text: Stone sink

definitions.meaning: a flat paving slab, a flagstone
to tire or droop, to lose energy

explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a paving slab, and to flag is to droop or weaken: two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Ignore port in a storm and founder

indicators.note: in a storm means the letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship that ignores the harbour in a storm will founder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founder' looks like the ship's sinking verb, but it is the noun: one who founds a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is an ancestor who founded a family line, a founder in that sense.

clue.text: Sauce containing cheese and tomato's first for serious quality

indicators.note: containing means the sauce word holds the cheese and letter inside it

parts.note: soy is a sauce, from soya beans
Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the tomato word

explanation.surface: A cook ponders a sauce of cheese with a hint of tomato, a solemn matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriety is seriousness, gravity, a quality of a sober and serious manner.

clue.text: Indulgent fool back in trouble

indicators.note: in places the turned fool word inside the trouble word

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or plague them

indicators.note: back means the fool word is read backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted parent's silly child is back in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means excessively fond and indulgent, as a doting grandparent is.
